SECTION 3: SITUATIONAL SALES SCENARIOS
SITUATION 1: First-Time Client Inquiry (Phone)
Scenario: Potential client calls asking about Botox pricing
Who Handles: Front Desk
Objectives:
●      Avoid pricing in isolation
●      Position value before cost
●      Secure consultation
●      Plant package/membership seed
Complete Script Flow:
Client: "Hi, how much is Botox?"
Front Desk: "Great question! I'm so glad you called. My name is [Name]. Who do I have the pleasure of speaking with?"
Client: "[Name]"
Front Desk: "Wonderful, [Name]. I love that you're thinking about this. Before I talk numbers, can I ask — is this your first time considering neurotoxin treatments, or have you had Botox before?"
Client Response A: "First time"
Front Desk: "Perfect! So here's what I recommend: Botox is typically priced per unit, and everyone needs a different amount based on their goals and muscle strength. Rather than throw a random number at you, let's get you in for a complimentary consultation with one of our injectors. They'll assess exactly what you need, show you what's possible, and give you precise pricing. Most clients find this way more helpful than a phone quote. Do mornings or afternoons work better for you?"
Client Response B: "I've had it before"
Front Desk: "Awesome! So you know how it works. Our pricing is $12 per unit, and most clients use between 20-60 units depending on the areas they treat. That said, we also offer packages and a membership that brings your cost down significantly — especially if you're maintaining this regularly. Would you like to come in and speak with an injector about a long-term plan, or would you prefer to just book a single treatment?"
Key Teaching Points:
●      Never give pricing without context
●      Always offer consultation for new clients
●      For returning clients, mention packages immediately
●      Use assumptive language ("when" not "if")

SITUATION 2: Client Books Single Treatment Online
Scenario: Client self-schedules a single laser hair removal session via website
Who Handles: Front Desk (confirmation call) → Consultant (day-of)
Objectives:
●      Educate on treatment series requirements
●      Position package before arrival
●      Set expectation for consultation upsell
Front Desk Confirmation Call Script:
Front Desk: "Hi [Name], this is [Your Name] from [Practice]. I'm calling to confirm your laser hair removal appointment on [Date] at [Time]. Do you have a quick second?"
Client: "Yes"
Front Desk: "Perfect! I just want to make sure you have the right expectations. Laser hair removal isn't a one-and-done treatment — it typically takes 6-8 sessions for permanent reduction. Most of our clients purchase a package upfront because it saves money and ensures they complete the full series. When you come in, your consultant will go over the options with you. Sound good?"
Client: "Okay, yes"
Front Desk: "Great! We'll see you [Day] at [Time]. Looking forward to meeting you!"
Day-of Consultant Script:
Consultant: "Hi [Name]! Welcome. I see you're here for laser hair removal. Have you done this before, or is this your first time?"
Client: "First time"
Consultant: "Perfect. So here's what you need to know: one session will reduce some hair, but you won't see permanent results. Hair grows in cycles, so we need to catch it multiple times. The gold standard is 6-8 treatments, spaced 4-6 weeks apart. We have a few options:
●      Single session: $350
●      Package of 6: $1,800 (saves $300)
●      Package of 8: $2,400 (saves $400 and ensures complete results)
Most clients go with the 6 or 8 because they want this done right. Which makes more sense for your goals?"
Key Teaching Points:
●      Educate before they arrive
●      Frame packages as the standard, not an upsell
●      Use savings language
●      Give clear options with recommendation

SITUATION 3: Client Hesitant About Package Pricing
Scenario: Client wants results but resists package investment
Who Handles: Consultant, Esthetician, Nurse, or Injector (whoever is presenting)
Objectives:
●      Reframe from cost to value
●      Break down cost-per-result
●      Offer payment plans
●      Compare to doing nothing
Complete Objection Handling Script:
Client: "That's more than I wanted to spend"
You: "I totally understand — I want to make sure you're comfortable. Can I ask, what were you thinking investment-wise?"
Client: "I was hoping to just do one and see"
You: "That makes sense, and you absolutely can. Here's what I want you to know: when clients do one treatment, they see some improvement, but it's temporary. Then they come back six months later and we're starting over. The clients who get the results they actually want are the ones who commit to the full series upfront. So it's less about spending more — it's about actually solving the problem versus just renting a solution. Does that make sense?"
Client: "Yeah, but I still don't know if I can afford it right now"
You: "Totally fair. We do offer payment plans — you can spread this over [X] months, which brings it down to about [Y] per month. That's less than most people spend on coffee. And honestly, if this is important to you, isn't it worth financing a real solution rather than wasting money on things that don't work?"

Client: "I just want to look better"
You: "Got it. So here's another option: we have a membership that spreads the cost out monthly and gets you access to multiple services at a lower rate. A lot of clients find that easier to budget for. Want me to walk you through it?"
Key Teaching Points:
●      Never argue, always empathize first
●      Reframe cost as investment in results
●      Offer payment plans immediately
●      Compare to cost of NOT solving the problem

SITUATION 4: Retail Recommendation During Facial
Scenario: Esthetician performing facial on client with visible hyperpigmentation
Who Handles: Esthetician
Objectives:
●      Tie retail to treatment outcomes
●      Position as essential, not optional
●      Recommend full routine, not single product
●      Overcome "I'll think about it"

Client: "Yeah, I've tried a few things but nothing really works"
Esthetician: "That makes sense — hyperpigmentation is stubborn. The good news is, what we're doing in-clinic today will help, but if we don't support it at home, the results won't last. I'm going to recommend a few products that actually work. Sound good?"
Client: "Sure"
At End of Treatment:

Vitamin C serum in the morning — this brightens and prevents new spots
Retinol at night — this accelerates cell turnover and fades existing spots
SPF 50 daily — because UV exposure will undo everything
These three together are what all my clients with hyperpigmentation use, and they see results in about 4-6 weeks. The investment is about $180 total, and these will last you 3-4 months. Do you want to start with the full routine or just pick one?"
Client: "That's expensive. Can I just get the Vitamin C?"
Esthetician: "You can, but here's the thing — if you only do one, you won't see the results you want. It's like going to the gym once a week and expecting a six-pack. These products work together. You're already investing in facials — let's make sure that investment actually pays off. If you get these today, I'll follow up with you in a month and we'll see what's working. Deal?"

●      Diagnose the problem during treatment
●      Recommend a complete system, not a single product
●      Tie to treatment they're already paying for
●      Overcome objections with truth and urgency

- Lifetime value beats transactional thinking
